synthesis.summary: Cross-dimension intersections show promo-driven conversion is strong but frequently blocked by caps/stock/code issues, while sensitive-skin positioning is simultaneously a demand driver and a safety/credibility risk when users still experience irritation.

findings.title: Promo-driven purchase intent is high, but conversion is blocked by code caps/stock and link friction
findings.business_implication: Heavy reliance on limited-cap discount mechanics creates frustrated would-be buyers and repeated 'where is link / code doesn't work' friction, risking lost sales and undermining campaign efficiency.
findings.recommended_action_area: Promo ops + comms: ensure stable inventory, clearer 'online only' messaging, visible links, real-time cap/stock status, and fallback offer once caps are hit.

findings.title: Sensitive-skin/anti-irritation claim attracts questions and intent, but real-world irritation reports create safety and credibility exposure
findings.business_implication: When a product is positioned as solving bumps/irritation, any counterexamples (rash/cuts/bumps) become disproportionately salient and can fuel skepticism about influencer claims.
findings.recommended_action_area: Claims & education: provide clearer usage guidance (pressure, direction, prep, aftercare), set expectations, and equip creators with troubleshooting + safety disclaimers and when-to-stop/seek care.

findings.title: Refills/extra blades and cashback process confusion is a repeat info gap that can suppress repeat purchase
findings.business_implication: Unclear refill availability and complicated cashback requirements increase drop-off post-trial, limiting lifetime value despite strong initial interest.
findings.recommended_action_area: Retail & CRM: improve refill findability (store locator, SKU naming consistency), simplify cashback instructions, and add post-purchase messages about where to buy refills.

faq_gaps.summary: Top information gaps: where to buy (country/retailer), replacement blades/refills, price, promo-code mechanics, and cashback submission rules/eligibility.

findings.title: Shaving skepticism drives substitution toward OneBlade/laser rather than Venus trial
findings.business_implication: When viewers perceive shaving as causing ingrowns/irritation or fast regrowth, they may bypass Venus entirely and move to alternative devices or longer-term hair removal methods.
findings.recommended_action_area: Messaging & education: address ingrowns/irritation prevention (prep, technique, aftercare) and clarify who shaving is best for vs when to consider alternatives.

findings.title: Ad skepticism + routine info gaps push creators into defensive clarification mode
findings.business_implication: If sponsorship clarity and product sourcing are not handled upfront, comments shift from product discussion to credibility debate and basic Q&A, reducing commercial efficiency of the placement.
findings.recommended_action_area: Creator guidance: standardize disclosure language and add pinned comments/product lists answering the top sourcing/routine questions.

faq_gaps.summary: Information gaps include: where to obtain a material/product (glue) in a Venus-tagged short, and routine questions like double cleansing and product sourcing—these suggest viewers need clearer product lists and sourcing guidance.

synthesis.summary: Key intersections show conversion being blocked by information gaps and code issues, and partnership skepticism intersecting with competitor switching and price/pink-tax objections. Brand safety risks also emerge around promotions/trust and influencer due diligence.

findings.title: High intent but blocked by info gaps (links, where-to-buy, code failures)
findings.business_implication: Users ready to buy are stalling due to missing purchase paths and promo code friction; lost conversions likely during short promo windows.
findings.recommended_action_area: Commerce enablement: standardized link-in-bio/UGC link replies, pinned availability FAQs, and proactive code troubleshooting/clarity.

findings.title: Partnership cynicism + competitor alternatives + price/pink-tax narratives reinforce switching away
findings.business_implication: When ads feel excessive or inconsistent, audiences invoke cheaper men’s razors/safety razors or rival brands (Estrid/Bic/Wilkinson), amplifying value skepticism and eroding ad effectiveness.
findings.recommended_action_area: Creator/brief strategy: reduce repetitive ad frequency, require usage-proof/consistency statements, and address value pricing (pink tax) head-on with transparent comparisons or bundles.

findings.title: Trust & compliance risk around promotions and influencer credibility ("scam" claims, 'fake doctor' accusations)
findings.business_implication: Allegations of scam/phishing and influencer misrepresentation can contaminate brand trust, increasing legal/reputational exposure and depressing conversion across markets.
findings.recommended_action_area: Risk management: rapid-response comms playbook, verified winner communications, clearer promo governance, and stricter influencer vetting/credentials policies.

findings.title: Irritation claims persist despite 'intimate' positioning, creating product-performance skepticism
findings.business_implication: If the core promise is reduced irritation but users still report bumps/rash, credibility weakens and drives method switching (wax/laser) and negative word-of-mouth.
findings.recommended_action_area: Product education + support: clearer technique guidance, post-shave regimen recommendations, and escalation pathways for adverse reaction reports.

faq_gaps.summary: Information gaps are dominated by where-to-buy, promo-code mechanics, cashback participation rules, and availability/compatibility questions.
